subroutines.name: main
subroutines.title: *RUN entry: decrypt and auto-run
subroutines.description:
The file system execution address (*RUN entry-point) for this
binary; it starts just past the decoy stub at &1900. Decrypts the resident
drivers and BASIC in place, writes the correct length byte back into the BASIC's
first line, then queues PAGE=&1C00 / OLD / RUN so the now-plain BASIC
configuration program starts.

subroutines.name: decode_basic
subroutines.title: Decrypt the resident drivers and BASIC
subroutines.description:
Rotate every byte of &1A00-&4AFF left one bit (the inverse of
the ROL-1 storage protection), in place. That covers both resident driver variants
(&1A00, &1B00) and the tokenised BASIC from PAGE=&1C00; the loop stops at page
&4B, leaving the BASIC's raw tail untouched.

subroutines.name: os_dependent_setup
subroutines.title: OS-version-dependent setup
subroutines.description: Reads the three-byte "OS " ROM signature to pick how the auto-run commands are queued.

subroutines.name: patch_header
subroutines.title: Repair the BASIC program's first line
subroutines.description:
Write &17 (23) into basic_line10_len, the length byte of the
line-10 REM at PAGE=&1C00, which is stored as 0 by the protection.

subroutines.name: queue_autorun
subroutines.title: Queue the auto-run commands (direct poke)
subroutines.description:
Copy autorun_commands into the MOS keyboard buffer so the OS
reads them as typed. autorun_index wraps into the 32-byte buffer at
&03E0-&03FF.

subroutines.name: setup_keys
subroutines.title: Queue the auto-run commands (OSBYTE path)
subroutines.description:
The non-"OS "-signature variant of queue_autorun: set the
BREAK/ESCAPE behaviour, then insert each autorun_commands byte with OSBYTE &8A.

memory_map.name: decode_ptr
memory_map.description: ROL-decode cursor sweeping the encrypted drivers and BASIC in place.

memory_map.name: autorun_index
memory_map.description: Running fill index into the keyboard buffer as the loader queues its PAGE / OLD / RUN commands.

memory_map.name: kbd_buffer
memory_map.description: Base of the &0300 page holding the MOS keyboard buffer, written directly on the fast hand-off path.

memory_map.name: os_signature
memory_map.description: Three OS ROM bytes read as the "OS " tag to distinguish OS versions and choose the command hand-off path.

memory_map.name: osbyte
memory_map.description: OSBYTE: used to read/set vectors and enable ADC input while the loader hands off to the BASIC.

comments_before_label: Decoy stub BASIC line (&0D, line 13, RTS bytes) so a naive *LOAD/LIST at PAGE sees junk, not the loader. It is 9 bytes (&1900-&1908); the exec address &1909 starts just past it. (KEYPAD has no such decoy: its file opens on the resident driver, and its loader sits in the tail at &3906.)

comments_before_label: Unused bytes after the command list, up to the resident driver at &1A00; referenced by nothing and inert.
Resident-driver template A, ROL-encoded (256 bytes; runs at &0A00). Disassembled in driver-a.asm.
Resident-driver template B, ROL-encoded (256 bytes; runs at &0A00). Disassembled in driver-b.asm.
Tokenised BASIC configuration program (PAGE=&1C00), ROL-encoded up to basic_raw_tail then stored raw. Source: basic/voltmace-delta-14b-driver-joystik.bas.
The loader stops decrypting here (page &4B): the rest of the BASIC is stored raw, beyond the decode range.

BBC BASIC's variable heap as it stood when the author saved the &1900-&4D00 image: variable-name/value records for the program globals (e.g. REV$="Rev 2.0", and LR%, R1%, EV$, LVL%, LVH%, S% ...). Not used by the loader; PAGE=&1C00 sits below it, so BASIC rebuilds its own variables on RUN.
